utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we can go ahead on that score. All right. There is the other matter of protective measure. There is the motion by the Defence for the granting of protective measures in relation to certain numbered witnesses. Leaving apart the question as to whether these will ultimately be brought over or not, which is none of my concern for the time being, but it is definitely the concern of the Defence and I need to protect these witnesses for the Defence if they are coming over. Do you have any objection that we grant the protective measures that are being sought by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I requested Ms. Patricia Sellers to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are in the course of responding in written form to this motion and we would certainly oppose this motion particularly in terms of the delayed disclosure of five of the Defence witnesses. The reason that we do oppose the delay disclosure is that Defence has proposed to only reveal their identity to the Prosecution. We are not talking about confidentiality within the public realm; we're talking about delaying the disclosure of their identity to the Prosecution at five different time periods, five different intervals, during the Defence case. And we would vigorously oppose that because we do need to prepare per witness, in terms of cross-examination, plus just knowing the identities of all of the Defence witnesses assists us in preparation for cross-examination of the witnesses. In terms of the other measures, Your Honour, for confidentiality, facial and voice distortion, while they testify, with the information that's been furnished to the Prosecutor at this point, we it would oppose it. We do understand it was an ex parte filing and that if there is other information that's before Your Honours that would make your decision different, we would then ask that those protective measures be appropriately tailored. With the information we have at this point we would have to say we oppose it. But I would like to say that it's a two-pronged approach that we had to their motion and we had intended to file that on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's very good to know because if you were not in a position to provide us with a feedback on it today, we were going to insist that you try and respond to the motion as early as possible before the usual time limit that would you have at your disposal under the rules. So I do appreciate that you will be coming back to us on that matter on Monday. The position will be as follows: We will see your response. If we need to address you any further - when I say you, the parties - any further on the matter, we will do so. If we don't, we will proceed with our decision. But this is an area where we cannot sleep on it. Also, because we don't know if any of these witnesses are amongst the ones that the Defence will be -- will be bringing forward, and maybe also at an early stage. So that I don't know. But we need to have this decided. All right? So we expect your response first thing Monday, please, so that we can work on it as quickly as we can. Let me go through the agenda ones more to see if we have left anything. Yes, yes, yes, yes, yes. Now, again, leaving apart this question of -- Mr. Jones, leaving apart this question of appeal or no appeal, that is up to you to decide, and, of course, it's -- we are not going to detract in any way from that right that you have except that, of course, we need to certify it. But I said already that if there is an appeal, it's not going to stop the progress of there case, which also basically means that you will need to provide us with a new witness list, witness list, and we would like you to file that by not later than Monday, the 11th of July. If you encounter problems, then please come back to us with a provisional list on those witnesses that you don't have any doubts, leaving out those witnesses where you are still undecided, and we will give you a further time, which will not be a long time, within which to conclude the list of 30 witnesses. Of course, the filing of this list will be without prejudice, and I don't need to explain that or even to say it aloud. You will be filing the list because you need to file the list, and it will not compromise at all your appeal. All right? So, yes, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, speaking about appeal, I'd like to put on the record that we also need time of course to respond to that, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course, but that -- the position is very simple, Mr. Wubben. I -- maybe I did not make myself clear. What I told

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES IS THIS
utterances.text: I'm not telling Mr. Jones we are going to certify it. But let's assume for the time being we will certify it. We are telling Mr. Jones the fact that you will appeal will not be of an impediment to the Prosecution of the Defence case. We will start it on Monday, and we will continue. It will also not be an impediment to the Prosecution of the Defence team if you require time to file your response to the appeal. Of course you will file a response. But that will be a problem of the Appeals Chamber to see whether to curtail on your time or not. What we will do is pass on a message to the Appeals Chamber that it is necessary for all of us to have the situation crystallised as early as possible so that both sides, and the Trial Chamber, will know whether we are on the right track or not, because if we are not -- in other words, if the Appeals Chamber comes to the conclusion, which is different to ours, then obviously we have to revise everything, we have to go through all this again, and decide when the case for the Prosecution will finish, how many witnesses they will have, because we still have to do that pursuant to Rule 73 ter. Just like we did with you in the pre-trial stage. You wanted more witnesses and we told you, no, Mr. Wubben, or whoever it was at the time, because it wasn't even myself. You will not be allowed these many. You will not have more than this amount of witnesses for this and this amount of witnesses for that, and that's it. So we are doing the same with the Defence, and in the case of the Defence, we are being extremely more cautious than we could afford to be with you, because with you, our interest is to make sure that you are allowed sufficient evidence to prove your case. With the Defence, there are very crucial rights involved, crucial rights involved, but we are in a situation where two counts are off. So -- yes. Is there any further business that you would like to transact today by way of Pre-Defence Conference?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And this is with a view to the operational matters for the coming week. Now, there will be a filing of provisional witness list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. And will there also be a modified exhibit list or anyhow, a confirmation that there will be no modification of it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben, I'm sure Mr. Jones is wiser on this. You will have noticed that I did not open my mouth on the exhibits that the Defence wishes to tender. And I am not going to open my mouth on that matter now. That's -- I said the way in which they would like to conduct their Defence is no -- of no concern to us. If they feel that their case is better served by 450 exhibits, that's not going to take from our trial time. It's going to take off time from our time because we will have to read and examine all those documents, which we will, like we will and we have already, examined all the documents that you have brought forward. We will do the same with the -- whether it's wise or not to have all those documents, it's their problem, not mine. So -- don't expect me to comment on that, and don't expect me to put any restrictions on the Defence on documentary evidence. What I would like them to do is to give you a copy, if they haven't, of the photographs and of the video, because I don't know if it's already the video that we have seen. I haven't got a clue. Please show it to the Prosecution so that if they don't have a question with the authenticity, you will also have an indication on whether you need to get those two witnesses over.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, we may first have to decide whether to call them at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Before we show the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is this last minor issue that's of importance for us. There is no, so far, no sequence order of the witnesses for the coming week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They will need to do that. No, for the coming week, I think there is. According to me, it is Edina.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Becirevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then I think it's the ex-SDA politician. Then I think it was that -- the Belgian doctor. Then last was the girl who was 15 years old at the time which we are telling you we are not interested in hearing her evidence because we think it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's confirmed by the Defence that that's the orders?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And more or less you also have an indication that one will be needed for five hours. That's the second person, the SDA member, five, if not more, and the other one is needed for hour hours, if not more, on examination-in-chief. So more or less you should -- more or less, but I expect you to sit down between now and Monday and organise yourself as to the schedule of witness testimony for the coming week, for the coming two weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: M'hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then of course, Mr. Jones and Madam Vidovic will have to adapt the same procedure we adapted before of handing to you beforehand a list of witnesses they will be showing up the week after or the weeks after, with the names and also the amount of hours they are expected to be in the witness stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I hope it will be in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, that's a matter of cooperation, but I expect you Mr. Jones and Mr. Wubben, please do meet on Monday and start to thresh these things out, of course without prejudice to your appeal. I thank you all.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just to say, I think it is clear, but Your Honour has indicated that one of the witnesses you don't think would be particularly necessary, so, of course, we will try and line up another -- another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You should try.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: As long as that's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You should try. That's your choice is -- will remain your choice. I mean, we are not going to tell you we consider this witness more important than the other because we can't do that. But I think by reading your own list, and by knowing who may be available, it's in your interest not to waste time. And any time lost not to -- due to any fault of your own will be recovered. So if on Monday we need to discuss for an hour urgent matters that may arise, you will be -- are going to be credited with the time lost. This is the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I only clarify it because obviously if we make a great effort to get another witness here in the next week or two, we trust that the Prosecution will bear with us and not of course raise objections that we've added a new witness a week before because of that. Of course, that's the position which we are forced into as of today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will hear what objections Mr. Wubben would have and then both of you would have to abide by our decision. This is -- we are not trying to bully you or to force our way but we are in a situation where we have to put discipline where we feel it is needed. So we may have to end up in that, Mr. Wubben. So you may come up and say, this is not fair, we are -- we may be in a position to say, yes, you are right, there will be no sitting on Thursday and on Friday, and we will credit those days to the Defence. Or else we can say, no, we can proceed, you may have a problem. Try to find a solution. So -- but I can't tell you from now what -- because I don't know who you are going to propose as the next witnesses. I haven't got an idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We have an idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I wish to thank you again publicly, thank you for the constructive way in which you have cooperated with the Trial Chamber. I know that the decision is one which is likely to cause indigestion, but we consider it as a necessary decision and you will receive it in writing on Monday. And then of course we will consider the question of certification.
